After analyzing the problems from real users, I've identified the top 5 startup opportunities for Nigerian university students. Here are the ideas:

**1.** **[IDEA NAME]**: DigiDoc
**PROBLEM**: Many users are looking for open-source alternatives to Notion or Outline for document management.
**SOLUTION**: A simple, user-friendly document management app with collaboration features, integrated with Google Drive or other cloud storage services.
**WHO PAYS**: Students, small businesses, and entrepreneurs who need affordable document management solutions.
**PRICE**: ₦500/month (basic plan) or ₦2,000/year (premium plan).
**FIRST WEEK**:
	1. Conduct market research to understand the needs of the target audience.
	2. Design a basic prototype of the app using existing open-source solutions.
	3. Set up a landing page to collect email addresses from interested users.
**WHY NOW**: With the increasing demand for open-source alternatives, DigiDoc can fill the gap in the Nigerian market.
**FEASIBILITY SCORES**:
	* Investment: 8/10 (using existing open-source solutions reduces development costs)
	* Passive Income: 6/10 (some manual work required for customer support and updates)
	* Team Size: 7/10 (can be developed with a small team, but may require additional help for marketing and support)
	* Time to Market: 8/10 (can be launched within a few weeks with a basic prototype)

**2.** **[IDEA NAME]**: RadarNG
**PROBLEM**: Some users are looking for innovative ways to track and monitor activities, such as flight radar or product reviews.
**SOLUTION**: A mobile app that provides real-time tracking and monitoring of Nigerian flights, buses, or other transportation services.
**WHO PAYS**: Commuters, travelers, and logistics companies who need to track shipments or vehicles.
**PRICE**: ₦200/transaction (basic plan) or ₦1,000/month (premium plan).
**FIRST WEEK**:
	1. Research existing APIs for flight and transportation data in Nigeria.
	2. Design a user-friendly interface for the app.
	3. Develop a basic prototype using existing APIs and frameworks.
**WHY NOW**: With the growing demand for transportation services in Nigeria, RadarNG can provide a unique solution for tracking and monitoring.
**FEASIBILITY SCORES**:
	* Investment: 9/10 (using existing APIs reduces development costs)
	* Passive Income: 8/10 (can be automated with minimal manual work)
	* Team Size: 8/10 (can be developed with a small team)
	* Time to Market: 9/10 (can be launched within a few weeks with a basic prototype)

**3.** **[IDEA NAME]**: ReviewNG
**PROBLEM**: Users are looking for Rotten Tomatoes-style platforms for durable products, but there's a lack of such platforms in Nigeria.
**SOLUTION**: A web and mobile app that allows users to review and rate Nigerian products, services, and businesses.
**WHO PAYS**: Businesses who want to improve their reputation and increase customer trust.
**PRICE**: ₦1,000/month (basic plan) or ₦5,000/month (premium plan).
**FIRST WEEK**:
	1. Conduct market research to understand the needs of Nigerian businesses and consumers.
	2. Design a user-friendly interface for the app.
	3. Develop a basic prototype using existing frameworks and APIs.
**WHY NOW**: With the growing e-commerce market in Nigeria, ReviewNG can provide a unique solution for businesses to improve their reputation and increase customer trust.
**FEASIBILITY SCORES**:
	* Investment: 8/10 (using existing frameworks and APIs reduces development costs)
	* Passive Income: 7/10 (some manual work required for moderation and updates)
	* Team Size: 7/10 (can be developed with a small team, but may require additional help for marketing and support)
	* Time to Market: 8/10 (can be launched within a few weeks with a basic prototype)

**4.** **[IDEA NAME]**: LibreTaxiNG
**PROBLEM**: Users are looking for free and open-source alternatives to Uber and Lyft, but there's a lack of such services in Nigeria.
**SOLUTION**: A mobile app that connects riders with drivers, using a peer-to-peer, open-source platform.
**WHO PAYS**: Riders who use the service, with a small commission fee.
**PRICE**: ₦100/ride (basic plan) or ₦500/ride (premium plan).
**FIRST WEEK**:
	1. Research existing open-source solutions for ride-hailing services.
	2. Design a user-friendly interface for the app.
	3. Develop a basic prototype using existing frameworks and APIs.
**WHY NOW**: With the growing demand for ride-hailing services in Nigeria, LibreTaxiNG can provide a unique, open-source solution.
**FEASIBILITY SCORES**:
	* Investment: 8/10 (using existing open-source solutions reduces development costs)
	* Passive Income: 6/10 (some manual work required for customer support and updates)
	* Team Size: 7/10 (can be developed with a small team, but may require additional help for marketing and support)
	* Time to Market: 8/10 (can be launched within a few weeks with a basic prototype)

**5.** **[IDEA NAME]**: DigiSafe
**PROBLEM**: Users are looking for end-to-end encrypted alternatives to Google Photos, but there's a lack of such services in Nigeria.
**SOLUTION**: A mobile app that provides end-to-end encrypted storage for photos, videos, and other files.
**WHO PAYS**: Individuals and businesses who need secure storage solutions.
**PRICE**: ₦500/month (basic plan) or ₦2,000/month (premium plan).
**FIRST WEEK**:
	1. Research existing solutions for end-to-end encryption.
	2. Design a user-friendly interface for the app.
	3. Develop a basic prototype using existing frameworks and APIs.
**WHY NOW**: With the growing demand for secure storage solutions in Nigeria, DigiSafe can provide a unique, end-to-end encrypted solution.
**FEASIBILITY SCORES**:
	* Investment: 9/10 (using existing solutions for end-to-end encryption reduces development costs)
	* Passive Income: 8/10 (can be automated with minimal manual work)
	* Team Size: 8/10 (can be developed with a small team)
	* Time to Market: 9/10 (can be launched within a few weeks with a basic prototype)

These ideas focus on zero-capital, passive income opportunities that can be developed with a small team. They address specific pain points in the Nigerian market and have the potential to scale and generate revenue.

As an experiment, we gave Claude Code the OOXML spec, a concrete editor architecture, and a Playwright-based test suite. The agent iterated in a (Ralph) loop over a few nights and produced a working editor from scratch.

Core text editing works today. Tables and images are functional but still incomplete. MIT licensed.

Typically claude code globs directories, greps for patterns, and reads files with minimal guidance. It works in kind of the same way you'd learn to navigate a city by walking every street. You'll eventually build a mental map, but claude never does - at least not any that persists across different contexts.

Show HN: CodeMic With CodeMic you can record and share coding sessions directly inside your editor.

Think Asciinema, but for full coding sessions with audio, video, and images.

While replaying a session, you can pause at any point, explore the code in your own editor, modify it, and even run it. This makes following tutorials and understanding real codebases much more practical than watching a video.

Local first, and open source.
